title: Pulse-pressure × pulse gives a small, uncertain log-CRP prediction gain beyond conventional hemodynamic measures
abstract: In 4,723 NHANES 2007–08 adults, we fit nonlinear blood-pressure/pulse models with and without a pulse-pressure-by-pulse interaction, then evaluated frozen models in 5,225 independently sampled 2009–10 adults. Weighted target mean squared log-CRP error decreased by 0.001258 (approximate 95% source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap interval -0.000669 to 0.002945), a 0.103% point improvement. Cubic and post-hoc confounder/curvature challenges retained only small point gains. The interval crosses zero: these data do not establish a reliable added inflammation marker. This is concurrent prediction, not future disease prediction or clinical validation.
